newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iranian, Japanese win top Cannes film award.
newsitem.headline: Iranian, Japanese win top Cannes film award.

text.p: Iranian Director Abbas Kiarostami for "The Taste of the Cherry" and Japanese Director Shohei Imamura for "The Eel" won a joint Golden Palm best film award at the 50th Cannes film festival on Sunday.
French actress Isabelle Adjani, the jury president, also announced a special 50th anniversary prize awarded to Egypt's Youssef Chahine for all his work.
"The Sweet Hereafter", by Canada's Atom Egoyan, won a runner-up Grand Jury Prize at the televised award ceremony.
Sean Penn was voted best actor for "She's so Lovely" by fellow American Nick Cassavetes, and Kathy Burke was voted best actress for "Nil by Mouth" by Britain's Gary Oldman.
Kiarostami, who was given the Tehran authorities' green light to come to the festival only at the last minute, had received a standing ovation at the screening of his film.

The gala award ceremony ended the festival's 50th birthday edition overshadowed by on-screen violence and off-screen censorship. Chinese authorities stopped Zhang Yimou from coming to Cannes to present his film "Keep Cool".
Critics said the quality of films had been only average, and there were no major discoveries outside the competition.
